sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, moments, and transitions of our 20s,
sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《20几岁的心理学》，在这个播客里，我们畅谈20几岁时经历的巨大变化、重要时刻和人生转型，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及这些对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of your 20s.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落，很高兴你能来到这里收听又一期节目，当然，我们要一起剖析20几岁的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk about ADHD.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊聊注意力缺陷多动障碍（ADHD）。

sentences.en: Getting diagnosed with ADHD as an adult can feel like both a revelation and a bit of a reckoning.
sentences.zh: 成年后才被诊断出患有ADHD，感觉既像是一场醍醐灌顶的启示，又有点像是一次清算。

sentences.en: It's this moment when everything about how you've moved through the world probably makes a lot more sense, but you also now have to learn all these new ways to manage.
sentences.zh: 在这个时刻，你过去在世俗中摸爬滚打的种种方式可能突然变得很好理解，但与此同时，你也必须开始学习各种全新的应对方法。

sentences.en: That is exactly the experience of today's guest, Chris Wang.
sentences.zh: 这正是今天我们的嘉宾克里斯·王（Chris Wang）的亲身经历。

sentences.en: She's the founder of Shimmer.
sentences.zh: 她是Shimmer的创始人。

sentences.en: It's an ADHD coaching platform that has helped thousands of adults better understand their brains, and she herself was diagnosed in her 20s after years of feeling
sentences.zh: 这是一个ADHD教练平台，已经帮助数千名成年人更好地了解自己的大脑，而她本人也是在20几岁时才被确诊的，此前她多年来一直觉得

sentences.en: like she was kind of doing life wrong, and the thing is, her story is actually not a unique one.
sentences.zh: 自己把生活过得一团糟，关键是，她的故事其实并不罕见。

sentences.en: I've heard from so many of you who have had the same experience, been through the same process.
sentences.zh: 我听到了很多听众的反馈，你们都有过相同的经历，走过相同的历程。

sentences.en: So today, I wanted to talk to her about practical strategies for managing your time, energy, focus, managing ADHD in your 20s, especially when traditional productivity advice
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我想和她聊聊管理时间、精力、专注力的实用策略，聊聊如何在20几岁应对ADHD，尤其是当传统的效率建议

sentences.en: maybe hasn't ever worked for you.
sentences.zh: 可能对你从来都不管用的时候。

sentences.en: I also want to explore love and dating with ADHD, why relationships can feel so intense, so confusing or addictive, how to handle romantic rejection,
sentences.zh: 我还想探讨患有ADHD之人的爱情与约会，为什么亲密关系会显得那么强烈、困惑或让人上瘾，如何处理浪漫关系中的拒绝，

sentences.en: but also just rejection in general, and how to feel like you're not too much in a world that is asking everybody to be a lot smaller.
sentences.zh: 以及如何应对生活中的一般性拒绝，还有在这个要求每个人都默默缩减自我的世界里，如何觉得自己并不是“戏太多”。

sentences.en: I love this conversation.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个话题。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，我们这就切入正题。

sentences.en: Chris Wang, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·王，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for coming on.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你来做客。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: You're an absolute icon.
sentences.zh: 你绝对是个偶像级人物。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, I'm so excited.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我太激动了。

sentences.en: Can you tell the listeners a little bit about yourself and what you do?
sentences.zh: 能跟听众们简单介绍一下你自己和你的工作吗？

sentences.en: I feel like I gave a little introduction before, but I'm like, you can say it in your own words, in the better words, probably.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我刚才已经做了个简单介绍，但我想说，你可以用你自己的话说，说得肯定比我好。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's better, but I'm Chris.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是不是更好，不过我是克里斯。

sentences.en: I'm the co-founder and CEO of Shimmer.
sentences.zh: 我是Shimmer的联合创始人兼首席执行官。

sentences.en: I am also a late diagnosed ADHD-er, so I was diagnosed with ADHD when I was 28, which I know we'll get into that a little bit, but it's been a whirlwind of a journey,
sentences.zh: 我也是成年后才确诊的ADHD患者，我是在28岁时被诊断出患有ADHD的，我知道我们待会儿会深入聊聊这个，但在应对这一诊断的同时创办Shimmer，这段旅程简直像旋风一样波澜起伏，

sentences.en: navigating that diagnosis while creating Shimmer, which is a behavioral support platform.
sentences.zh: 这是一个行为支持平台。

sentences.en: And as of date, we've done 75,000 coaching sessions, which is really exciting.
sentences.zh: 截至目前，我们已经完成了75,000次教练辅导，这真的让人非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Just thinking about how many people have, with ADHD, have been a part of our journey, and many of them are late diagnosed as well.
sentences.zh: 只要一想到有多少患有ADHD的人曾参与到我们的旅程中，其中许多人也是成年后才确诊的，就感慨万千。

sentences.en: And the last piece is along the journey.
sentences.zh: 最后一个部分是关于这一路走来的历程。

sentences.en: This is very ADHD as well.
sentences.zh: 这也非常符合ADHD的特点。

sentences.en: Usually things kind of unfold.
sentences.zh: 通常事情就是顺其自然地展开了。

sentences.en: I have become an ADHD creator as well.
sentences.zh: 我也成了一位ADHD内容创作者。

sentences.en: So I started off by posting just, my first series was ADHD girl hacks.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始我只是发帖，我的第一个系列是“ADHD女孩小妙招”。

sentences.en: So posting hacks that I've gleaned through my coaching journey, and also those of the thousands of other folks who have gone through our platform,
sentences.zh: 分享我在自己的教练之旅中收集到的实用小技巧，以及通过我们平台受益的数千名其他伙伴的经验，

sentences.en: but since then have done ADHD girl works,
sentences.zh: 但自那以后，我还做了“ADHD女孩工作坊”、

sentences.en: ADHD girl dates, and ADHD girl feels.
sentences.zh: “ADHD女孩约会指南”和“ADHD女孩情感感悟”。

sentences.en: So I know we'll get into tips and things like that afterwards, but it's been a little bit of a journey since that diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们随后会讨论各种技巧之类的话题，但自从确诊以来，这段旅程确实经历了不少波折。

sentences.en: I'm really excited to hear about ADHD girl dates.
sentences.zh: 我特别期待听听关于“ADHD女孩约会指南”的内容。

sentences.en: That's like something
sentences.zh: 这就像是某种

sentences.en: I'm particularly interested in hearing, but this definitely won't surprise you.
sentences.zh: 我格外有兴趣听的内容，不过这绝对不会让你感到意外。

sentences.en: It did surprise me
sentences.zh: 确实让我感到意外的是，

sentences.en: how many people reach out to me with a similar story of like,
sentences.zh: 有多少人向我倾诉着相似的故事，比如：

sentences.en: I had all of these difficulties, or actually like sometimes even a lack of difficulties when I was at school.
sentences.zh: 我在学校时遇到了所有这些困难，或者实际上有时候甚至在学校时没遇到什么困难。

sentences.en: And then suddenly I became an adult, and, you know, all the things that people had ignored or that I'd like worked really hard to mask, like kind of came to the surface.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间我成年了，你知道的，大家曾经忽视的或者我曾拼命掩饰的所有问题，全都浮出水面了。

sentences.en: And here I was at 27, 28, 29, like basically discovering a new aspect of my identity and of how I operate.
sentences.zh: 于是27岁、28岁、29岁的我，基本上是在探索我身份的一个新维度以及我运转方式的新层面。

sentences.en: Can you tell us a little bit about your story and maybe like what it felt like or how it was growing up?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们讲讲你的故事吗？比如成长过程中感觉是怎样的，或者说经历过什么？

sentences.en: Did you feel different?
sentences.zh: 你觉得自己与众不同吗？

sentences.en: And when you maybe realized that like there was a label for this or a series of symptoms that could kind of explain it?
sentences.zh: 你是何时意识到这其实有一个专有名词，或者有一系列能够解释这种状况的症状的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I will first preface by saying that people's ADHD looks really different.
sentences.zh: 所以我首先要说明的是，每个人的ADHD表现形式真的很不一样。

sentences.en: And I'm glad you're asking for individual stories because I think sometimes it's very easy to hear a story and not hear yourself in it or hear a story and do hear yourself in it
sentences.zh: 很高兴你问及个人的故事，因为我觉得有时人们很容易听到一个故事却在其中找不到自己，或者听到一个故事却对号入座，

sentences.en: and feel like you either don't have ADHD or have ADHD.
sentences.zh: 从而觉得要么自己没有ADHD，要么自己确实有ADHD。

sentences.en: So I think it's really important to learn about the symptoms, learn about the different ways the symptoms can coexist with each other and also go through that process yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得了解这些症状、了解症状之间如何共存以及自己去经历这个过程真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And I also will want to say if your listeners haven't really dug into ADHD, there's also three types of ADHD and I'll share which one I am as well.
sentences.zh: 我还想说的是，如果你的听众还没有深入了解过ADHD，其实ADHD有三种类型，我也会分享我是哪一种。

sentences.en: But there's the hyperactive, impulsive ADHD, which are folks who as a kid were kind of bouncing off of walls, super talkative, probably getting into trouble.
sentences.zh: 首先是多动冲动型ADHD，这类人群在小时候往往精力极其旺盛，像停不下来一样，超级健谈，可能经常惹麻烦。

sentences.en: And as adults generally won't look as disruptive, but maybe it's chatty, maybe it's more internally being more hyperactive.
sentences.zh: 长大成年后，通常看起来没那么具有破坏性了，但可能表现为话多，或者内心更加多动。

sentences.en: And so that's kind of on the hyperactive, impulsive side.
sentences.zh: 这就是多动、冲动这一侧的情况。

sentences.en: And then there's the inattentive side, which is the other type that generally a lot of the times women will have and girls will have, which a lot of the times when you're younger
sentences.zh: 然后是注意力不集中型，这是另一种类型，女性和女孩往往更容易表现出这种类型，很多时候在年纪较小的时候，

sentences.en: will be internally presenting as well.
sentences.zh: 也是在内部表现出来。

sentences.en: So those are the daydreamers, the ones who maybe as an adult struggle to follow conversations or get lost in your own daydreams in your head.
sentences.zh: 所以这类人就是白日梦想家，他们可能在成年后很难跟上谈话的节奏，或者容易在自己的白日梦里迷失方向。

sentences.en: And so that inattentive ADHD will look really different from the hyperactive ADHD.
sentences.zh: 因此，注意力不集中型的ADHD跟多动型的ADHD表现会非常不同。

sentences.en: And the third type, which is the type that I am, fortunately or unfortunately, is the combined type.
sentences.zh: 至于第三种类型，也就是我所属的类型，不知是幸还是不幸，是混合型。

sentences.en: So that's when you have symptoms from both sides.
sentences.zh: 这就是你同时具备两边症状的情况。

sentences.en: And so when you meet someone who's has ADHD, they could look really different if they just fall within those three buckets, but also if they have other sorts of intersectionalities
sentences.zh: 所以当你遇到一个患有ADHD的人时，如果他们刚好落在这三种分类中，或者他们还有其他各种交织的身份特征，

sentences.en: and co-occurrences with other mental health conditions.
sentences.zh: 以及与其他心理健康状况的共病，他们的表现可能会大不相同。

sentences.en: So I just want to preface that.
sentences.zh: 所以我先做个这样的铺垫。

sentences.en: And so for me, I have all the most of the symptoms, but specifically the ones that were the most salient when I was a kid was definitely on the hyperactive side.
sentences.zh: 对我而言，我具备绝大多数症状，但特别是在我小时候最突出的那些，绝对是在多动这一侧。

sentences.en: I was super talkative.
sentences.zh: 我超级爱说话。

sentences.en: I was constantly distracting people around me.
sentences.zh: 我总是打扰周围的人。

sentences.en: I was always being told I was too loud or just to sit down or be quiet, just constantly in the way.
sentences.zh: 我总是被告知我太吵了，或者让我坐下、安静点，总觉得我到处碍事。

sentences.en: I think as I grew up,
sentences.zh: 我想随着我长大，

sentences.en: I've been thinking about this a lot.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: I think I've heard a lot of stories of folks who their self-confidence and anxiety just really increases over time, especially as girls.
sentences.zh: 我听到过很多这样的故事：随着时间的推移，人们的自信心和焦虑感会不断增加，尤其是女孩子。

sentences.en: And so there's actually the stat that people with ADHD hear 20,000 more negative messages by the time that they're 10 years old in comparison to their non-ADHD peers,
sentences.zh: 事实上有一个统计数据：患有ADHD的人到10岁时，与没有ADHD同龄人相比，会多听到2万条负面评价，

sentences.en: which is pretty significant.
sentences.zh: 这个数字相当惊人。
